claim: Gram-negative bacteria import essential nutrients such as iron and vitamin B12 through outer membrane receptors.
source: Gram-negative bacteria import essential nutrients such as iron and vitamin B12 through outer membrane receptors.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in microbiology supported by the citations in the manuscript and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: The nutrient import process utilizes proton motive force harvested by the Ton system made up of three inner membrane proteins, ExbB, ExbD and TonB.
source: This process utilizes proton motive force harvested by the Ton system made up of three inner membrane proteins, ExbB, ExbD and TonB.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: ExbB and ExbD form the proton channel that energizes uptake through TonB.
source: ExbB and ExbD form the proton channel that energizes uptake through TonB.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data and citations in the manuscript.

claim: Crystal structures suggest that the ExbB pentamer is the scaffold.
source: Recently, crystal structures suggest that the ExbB pentamer is the scaffold.
evidence: This refers to previously published crystal structures cited in the manuscript.

claim: Hexameric complexes of ExbB and ExbD were revealed by X-ray crystallography and single particle cryo-EM.
source: Here, we present structures of hexameric complexes of ExbB and ExbD revealed by X-ray crystallography and single particle cryo-EM.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the Results section.

claim: Hexameric and pentameric complexes coexist.
source: Image analysis shows that hexameric and pentameric complexes coexist, with the proportion of hexamer increasing with pH.
evidence: This is supported by cryo-EM image analysis data presented in Figure 4 and related text.

claim: The proportion of hexamer increases with pH.
source: Image analysis shows that hexameric and pentameric complexes coexist, with the proportion of hexamer increasing with pH.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4C and Supplementary file 1-Table S2.

claim: Channel current measurement supports the existence and transition of the two oligomeric states in membranes.
source: Channel current measurement and 2D crystallography support the existence and transition of the two oligomeric states in membranes.
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data presented in Figure 3.

claim: 2D crystallography supports the existence and transition of the two oligomeric states in membranes.
source: Channel current measurement and 2D crystallography support the existence and transition of the two oligomeric states in membranes.
evidence: This is supported by 2D crystal data presented in Figure 5.

claim: The hexameric complex consists of six ExbB subunits and three ExbD transmembrane helices enclosed within the central channel.
source: The hexameric complex consists of six ExbB subunits and three ExbD transmembrane helices enclosed within the central channel.
evidence: This is a primary structural finding supported by cryo-EM data shown in Figure 6.

claim: ATP synthesis is coupled to ion potentials across the lipid membrane.
source: Many essential biological processes are coupled to ion potentials across the lipid membrane. These include, amongst others, ATP synthesis (Junge et al., 2009)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by the citation to Junge et al., 2009.

claim: Uptake of nutrients is coupled to ion potentials across the lipid membrane.
source: Many essential biological processes are coupled to ion potentials across the lipid membrane. These include, amongst others, ATP synthesis (Junge et al., 2009), uptake of nutrients (Faraldo-Gómez and Sansom, 2003; Noinaj et al., 2010; Krewulak and Vogel, 2011; Abramson et al., 2003)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Protein secretion is coupled to ion potentials across the lipid membrane.
source: Many essential biological processes are coupled to ion potentials across the lipid membrane. These include, amongst others, ATP synthesis (Junge et al., 2009), uptake of nutrients (Faraldo-Gómez and Sansom, 2003; Noinaj et al., 2010; Krewulak and Vogel, 2011; Abramson et al., 2003), protein secretion (Tsukazaki et al., 2011)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by the citation to Tsukazaki et al., 2011.

claim: Multi-drug excretion is coupled to ion potentials across the lipid membrane.
source: Many essential biological processes are coupled to ion potentials across the lipid membrane. These include, amongst others, ATP synthesis (Junge et al., 2009), uptake of nutrients (Faraldo-Gómez and Sansom, 2003; Noinaj et al., 2010; Krewulak and Vogel, 2011; Abramson et al., 2003), protein secretion (Tsukazaki et al., 2011), multi-drug excretion (Murakami et al., 2006)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by the citation to Murakami et al., 2006.

claim: Rotation of the flagellar motor is coupled to ion potentials across the lipid membrane.
source: Many essential biological processes are coupled to ion potentials across the lipid membrane. These include, amongst others, ATP synthesis (Junge et al., 2009), uptake of nutrients (Faraldo-Gómez and Sansom, 2003; Noinaj et al., 2010; Krewulak and Vogel, 2011; Abramson et al., 2003), protein secretion (Tsukazaki et al., 2011), multi-drug excretion (Murakami et al., 2006), and rotation of the flagellar motor (Kojima, 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by the citation to Kojima, 2015.

claim: The Ton complex in gram-negative bacteria depends on proton motive force.
source: The Ton complex (Faraldo-Gómez and Sansom, 2003; Noinaj et al., 2010; Krewulak and Vogel, 2011) in gram-negative bacteria is an interesting example of a molecular machine that depends on proton motive force (PMF).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The Ton system conveys transmembrane energy to the distant outer membrane, ~20 nm away from the energy source sited at the inner membrane.
source: While other systems use this transmembrane (TM) energy at source (that is at the membrane with the proton gradient) the Ton system conveys it to the distant outer membrane, ~20 nm away from the energy source sited at the inner membrane (Du et al., 2014; Matias et al., 2003) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Ton complex is composed of three proteins ExbB, ExbD and TonB located in the inner membrane.
source: The Ton complex is composed of three proteins ExbB, ExbD and TonB located in the inner membrane.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the composition of the Ton complex.

claim: The Ton complex utilizes PMF to take up diverse compounds such as iron-loaded siderophores, haem, and vitamin B12 through outer membrane receptors.
source: It utilizes PMF to take up diverse compounds such as iron-loaded siderophores, haem, and vitamin B12 through outer membrane receptors (Faraldo-Gómez and Sansom, 2003; Noinaj et al., 2010; Krewulak and Vogel, 2011; Schauer et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Toxins such as colicin and some antibiotics, as well as phages, hijack the Ton system to gain entry to cells.
source: Toxins such as colicin and some antibiotics, as well as phages, hijack the Ton system to gain entry to these cells (Noinaj et al., 2010; Krewulak and Vogel, 2011; Schauer et al., 2008; Lloubès et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The Ton system could perhaps be used, through drug targeting, to attack pathogenic gram-negative bacteria.
source: It could perhaps be used, through drug targeting, to attack pathogenic gram-negative bacteria (Neelapu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential applications, supported by a citation.

claim: In response to proton flux through the Ton complex, the C-terminal domain of TonB interacts with TonB-dependent outer membrane receptors, which bind specific substrates.
source: In response to proton flux through the Ton complex, the C-terminal domain of TonB interacts with TonB-dependent outer membrane receptors, which bind specific substrates.
evidence: This describes the mechanism of the Ton system based on established knowledge.

claim: A conformational change releases the bound substrate from the receptor into the periplasmic space.
source: A conformational change releases the bound substrate from the receptor into the periplasmic space.
evidence: This describes the mechanism of substrate release based on established knowledge.

claim: Each substrate is then transported into the cell by its specific inner membrane transporters and related proteins.
source: Each substrate is then transported into the cell by its specific inner membrane transporters and related proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the subsequent transport step, illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Ton complex initiates the process and works as the energizer for outer membrane substrate uptake.
source: In all cases, the Ton complex initiates the process and works as the energizer for outer membrane substrate uptake.
evidence: This summarizes the role of the Ton complex based on established knowledge.

claim: ExbB has three TM helices with a large cytoplasmic domain.
source: ExbB has three TM helices with a large cytoplasmic domain (Celia et al., 2016)
evidence: This is supported by the citation to Celia et al., 2016 and confirmed by the structural data in this study.

claim: Both ExbD and TonB are predicted to have single TM helices and a compact periplasmic domain.
source: both ExbD and TonB are predicted to have single TM helices and a compact periplasmic domain (Garcia-Herrero et al., 2007; Ködding et al., 2005).
evidence: This is based on predictions supported by citations.

claim: ExbB and ExbD together form a proton channel.
source: ExbB and ExbD together form a proton channel
evidence: This is supported by experimental evidence cited in the manuscript.

claim: Isolated ExbBD complexes show ion conductivity and cation selectivity in vitro.
source: isolated ExbBD complexes show ion conductivity and cation selectivity in vitro (Celia et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by the citation to Celia et al., 2016 and confirmed by data in Figure 3 of this study.

claim: The ExbBD complex can be thought of as the engine and TonB a drive shaft connecting the engine to the gate in the outer membrane.
source: The ExbBD complex can be thought of as the engine and TonB a drive shaft connecting the engine to the gate in the outer membrane.
evidence: This is an analogy used to describe the functional relationship between components.

claim: MotAB/PomAB, TolQR, and AglRQS exhibit sequence homology to ExbBD.
source: Other channel complexes such as MotAB/PomAB (Kojima, 2015), TolQR (Lloubès et al., 2012; Godlewska et al., 2009), and AglRQS (Agrebi et al., 2015) exhibit sequence homology to ExbBD
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: MotAB/PomAB, TolQR, and AglRQS utilize ion motive force.
source: Other channel complexes such as MotAB/PomAB (Kojima, 2015), TolQR (Lloubès et al., 2012; Godlewska et al., 2009), and AglRQS (Agrebi et al., 2015) exhibit sequence homology to ExbBD and also utilize ion motive force
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: MotAB and PomAB generate torque for flagellar rotation.
source: MotAB and PomAB generate torque for flagellar rotation
evidence: This is established knowledge about the function of these complexes.

claim: TolQR maintains outer membrane integrity.
source: TolQR maintains outer membrane integrity
evidence: This is established knowledge about the function of TolQR.

claim: AglRQS energizes surface gliding and sporulation in slime bacteria.
source: AglRQS energizes surface gliding and sporulation in slime bacteria.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the function of AglRQS.

claim: Crystal structures of the ExbB pentamer with and without a short segment of ExbD including the TM region have been solved.
source: Although structural information on this family is limited, recently crystal structures of the ExbB pentamer with and without a short segment of ExbD including the TM region have been solved, giving valuable insights into the architecture of the ExbB complex.
evidence: This refers to previously published structures.

claim: A pentameric functional unit seems not to fit with previous studies.
source: However, a pentameric functional unit seems not to fit with previous studies (Higgs et al., 2002; Jana et al., 2011; Pramanik et al., 2011; Sverzhinsky et al., 2014; Sverzhinsky et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison with multiple previous studies.

claim: Formation of the hexamer is promoted at higher pH.
source: Formation of the hexamer is promoted at higher pH, in line with an increased macroscopic channel conductance.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Formation of the hexamer is in line with an increased macroscopic channel conductance.
source: Formation of the hexamer is promoted at higher pH, in line with an increased macroscopic channel conductance.
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data in Figure 3.

claim: Escherichia coli full-length ExbB-ExbD complexes were expressed and purified.
source: We expressed and purified Escherichia coli full-length ExbB-ExbD complexes.
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure performed in this study.

claim: The structure of crystals grown at pH 9.0 was solved to 2.8 Å by molecular replacement.
source: The structure of crystals grown at pH 9.0 was solved to 2.8 Å by molecular replacement.
evidence: This is a primary result of the crystallographic analysis.

claim: The asymmetric unit in the lattice with space group P21 contains two ExbB hexamers, one disposed upside down with respect to the other, and interacting laterally with each other.
source: The asymmetric unit in the lattice with space group P21 (Supplementary file 1-Table S1) contains two ExbB hexamers, one disposed upside down with respect to the other, and interacting laterally with each other (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This describes the crystal packing observed in the structure, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The overall hexamer structure resembles a bell with a vertical dimension of ~110 Å and a maximal horizontal dimension on the cytoplasmic side of ~85 Å.
source: The overall hexamer structure resembles a bell with a vertical dimension of ~110 Å and a maximal horizontal dimension on the cytoplasmic side of ~85 Å (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the dimensions of the hexamer structure determined in this study, shown in Figure 1.

claim: The proportion of ExbD tended to decrease upon crystallization.
source: The proportion of ExbD tended to decrease upon crystallization, as deduced from SDS-PAGE patterns of crystal samples (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an observation from SDS-PAGE analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Peptide mass finger printing analysis showed that some ExbD is retained in the crystals.
source: Yet, peptide mass finger printing analysis showed that some ExbD is retained in the crystals.
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry analysis of crystal samples.

claim: A Fourier difference map revealed untraceable masses, probably parts of ExbD TM helices, inside the channel of the hexamer.
source: A Fourier difference map revealed untraceable masses, probably parts of ExbD TM helices, inside the channel of the hexamer.
evidence: This is an observation from crystallographic analysis with an inference about the identity of the masses.

claim: Low occupancy and possibly flexibility may account for the lack of clarity of ExbD in the crystal structure.
source: Low occupancy and possibly flexibility may account for the lack of clarity.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observation.

claim: The ExbB monomers in the hexamer show similar structures to those in the pentamer (the average RMSD of Cα atoms between two monomers is 1.4 Å).
source: The ExbB monomers in the hexamer show similar structures to those in the pentamer (the average RMSD of Cα atoms between two monomers is 1.4 Å), despite the different subunit number (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison between structures shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Each ExbB monomer consists of three long α-helices (80 ~ 100 Å), one of which is broken at its middle in the cytoplasm, extending across the cytoplasmic and periplasmic spaces, and connected with short α-helices and loops; in total 7 α-helices (α1 - α7 from the N-terminus) are in each monomer.
source: The structure has been described previously (Celia et al., 2016), and, briefly, consists of three long α-helices (80 ~ 100 Å), one of which is broken at its middle in the cytoplasm, extending across the cytoplasmic and periplasmic spaces, and connected with short α-helices and loops; in total 7 α-helices (α1 - α7 from the N-terminus) are in each monomer.
evidence: This describes the structure of the ExbB monomer based on previous work and confirmed in this study.

claim: The TM region is well conserved over species.
source: The TM region is well conserved over species (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is based on sequence conservation analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The hexamer and pentamer form similar funnel structures with large cytoplasmic and smaller periplasmic domains connected through the TM region.
source: The hexamer and pentamer form similar funnel structures with large cytoplasmic and smaller periplasmic domains connected through the TM region (Figures 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a structural comparison shown in the figures.

claim: The overall volume is ~60,400 Å3 in the hexamer with an outermost diameter of ~85 Å on the cytoplasmic side.
source: The overall volume is ~60,400 Å3 in the hexamer with an outermost diameter of ~85 Å on the cytoplasmic side
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the structure.

claim: The overall volume is ~43,900 Å3 in the pentamer with an outermost diameter of ~75 Å on the cytoplasmic side.
source: ~43,900 Å3 and ~75 Å respectively in the pentamer.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the pentamer structure.

claim: The channel at center is surrounded by TM helices α6 and α7 in the membrane region and α5 and α7 further down.
source: The channel at center is surrounded by TM helices α6 and α7 in the membrane region and α5 and α7 further down (Figures 1, 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the structural arrangement shown in the figures.

claim: The channel in the hexamer is significantly larger than that in the pentamer.
source: The channel in the hexamer is significantly larger than that in the pentamer (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The diameter in the hexamer is ~17 Å through the TM region.
source: The diameter in the hexamer is ~17 Å and that in the pentamer ~10 Å through the TM region.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the structure.

claim: The diameter in the pentamer is ~10 Å through the TM region.
source: The diameter in the hexamer is ~17 Å and that in the pentamer ~10 Å through the TM region.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the pentamer structure.

claim: The pentamer structure of the crystal grown at pH 4.5 resolved one rod-like density located in the central channel towards the periplasm, and a part of the rod was assigned to a TM segment of ExbD.
source: The pentamer structure of the crystal grown at pH 4.5 resolved one rod-like density located in the central channel towards the periplasm, and a part of the rod was assigned to a TM segment of ExbD (Celia et al., 2016).
evidence: This refers to findings from the previous pentamer structure.

claim: The channel of the pentamer can accommodate only one helix, whereas that of the hexamer has multiple helices.
source: The channel of the pentamer can accommodate only one helix, whereas that of the hexamer has multiple helices.
evidence: This is a structural comparison based on the data in this study.

claim: The larger central channel in the hexamer would fit better with a multimerizing nature of ExbD.
source: The larger central channel in the hexamer would fit better with a multimerizing nature of ExbD (Higgs et al., 2002; Ollis et al., 2009; Gresock et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural data and previous studies.

claim: In both complexes, the large cytoplasmic domain has a cluster of positively charged residues surrounding the channel close to the membrane surface and a group of negatively-charged residues at the end on the cytoplasmic side.
source: In both complexes, the large cytoplasmic domain has a cluster of positively charged residues surrounding the channel close to the membrane surface and a group of negatively-charged residues at the end on the cytoplasmic side (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This describes the electrostatic properties shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Neighboring monomers of ExbB in the hexamer and in the pentamer bury approximately the same surface areas (3000 Å2).
source: Neighboring monomers of ExbB in the hexamer and in the pentamer bury approximately the same surface areas (3000 Å2)
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from structural analysis.

claim: The residues contributing to interactions between neighboring monomers are similar in hexamer and pentamer.
source: the residues contributing to interactions are also similar.
evidence: This is based on structural comparison.

claim: The negatively charged amino acids in the acidic cluster at the cytoplasmic end are further apart in the hexamer.
source: the negatively charged amino acids in the acidic cluster at the cytoplasmic end are further apart in the hexamer, and the channel radius is particularly large here (Figures 1D, 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is a structural observation shown in the figures.

claim: Lower pH increases chances for hydration of ionised acidic residues, which may allow the denser packing of the pentamer.
source: Lower pH increases chances for hydration of ionised acidic residues, which may allow the denser packing here of the pentamer.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the pH-dependent oligomerization.

claim: Deletion of residues 100–109, which include four acidic residues (Asp 102, Asp 103, Glu 105, and Glu 109) decreases iron transport activity.
source: This region is important for function, as deletion of residues 100–109, which include four acidic residues (Asp 102, Asp 103, Glu 105, and Glu 109) decreases iron transport activity (Bulathsinghala et al., 2013).
evidence: This is based on a previous functional study.

claim: Well-diffracting crystals of pentamers at pH 7.0 or lower were obtained following treatment of ExbB with a methyl-reducing reagent to modify the amide in lysine side chains.
source: It should be noted that in the previous structure study, well-diffracting crystals of pentamers at pH 7.0 or lower were obtained following treatment of ExbB with a methyl-reducing reagent to modify the amide in lysine side chains (Celia et al., 2016).
evidence: This refers to the methods used in the previous pentamer structure study.

claim: The modified lysine near Glu 109 and a calcium ion bound to all five Glu 105 side chains appeared to be needed for pentamer formation in the crystals.
source: Indeed, the modified lysine near Glu 109 and a calcium ion bound to all five Glu 105 side chains appeared to be needed for pentamer formation in the crystals (Figure 2d of Celia et al., 2016).
evidence: This refers to observations from the previous pentamer structure.

claim: The crystals in this study do not need treatment with a methyl-reducing reagent.
source: Our crystals do not need such treatment.
evidence: This describes a difference in crystallization conditions compared to the previous study.

claim: The channel conductance of ExbBD complexes reconstituted into planar lipid bilayers was measured.
source: We measured the channel conductance of ExbBD complexes reconstituted into planar lipid bilayers.
evidence: This describes an experimental procedure performed in this study.

claim: The behaviour of the channel is similar to that reported in Celia et al., 2016: The conductance shows high pH dependence, poor at low pH and greater at neutral pH or above.
source: The behaviour of the channel is similar to that reported in Celia et al., 2016: The conductance shows high pH dependence, poor at low pH and greater at neutral pH or above (Figure 3; Celia et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a comparison with previous results, confirmed by data in Figure 3.

claim: Frozen-hydrated specimens of ExbBD complexes purified at various pHs were examined with cryo-EM.
source: We then examined frozen-hydrated specimens of ExbBD complexes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B) purified at various pHs with cryo-EM.
evidence: This describes an experimental procedure performed in this study.

claim: Reference-free 2D class average of molecular images produced characteristic projections including hexameric and pentameric structures corresponding to projections normal to the membrane plane.
source: Reference-free 2D class average of molecular images produced characteristic projections (Figures 4A, B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and E). They include hexameric and pentameric structures corresponding to projections normal to the membrane plane.
evidence: This describes the results of cryo-EM image analysis shown in the figures.

claim: The hexameric and pentameric images resolve axial projections of the α-helices and well resemble the crystal structures viewed from the same direction.
source: The hexameric and pentameric images resolve axial projections of the α-helices and well resemble the crystal structures viewed from the same direction (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is a comparison between cryo-EM images and crystal structures shown in Figure 4.

claim: Complexes of ExbB pentamer and hexamer coexist in the sample solution and the proportion of each depends on pH, being 3:1 at pH 5.4, 1:3 at pH 8.0, and almost entirely hexamers at pH 9.0.
source: Complexes of ExbB pentamer and hexamer coexist in the sample solution and the proportion of each depends on pH, being 3:1 at pH 5.4, 1:3 at pH 8.0, and almost entirely hexamers at pH 9.0 (Figure 4C and Supplementary file 1-Table S2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from cryo-EM image analysis shown in Figure 4C and Supplementary file 1-Table S2.

claim: A previous MS analysis showed that the main fraction of the sample in the weak basic condition used corresponded to ExbB hexamers and small amounts of the pentamer were also found.
source: A previous MS analysis showed that the main fraction of the sample in the weak basic condition used corresponded to ExbB hexamers and small amounts of the pentamer were also found (Pramanik et al., 2011).
evidence: This refers to findings from a previous study.

claim: The proportion of hexamers and pentamers found in the previous MS analysis is consistent with the results of this study.
source: This proportion is consistent with our results (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a comparison between the current results and previous findings.

claim: 2D crystals were prepared at pH 5.4 by reconstituting purified ExbBD complexes into liposomes.
source: We prepared 2D crystals at pH 5.4 by reconstituting purified ExbBD complexes into liposomes.
evidence: This describes an experimental procedure performed in this study.

claim: Fourier filtering of different patches from negatively-stained 2D crystals revealed pentagonal and hexagonal images.
source: Fourier filtering of different patches from negatively-stained 2D crystals revealed pentagonal and hexagonal images (Figure 5).
evidence: This describes the results of 2D crystal analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: The coexistence of pentamers and hexamers probably prevents growth of well-diffracting crystals at pH 5.4.
source: The coexistence of pentamers and hexamers probably prevents growth of well-diffracting crystals at pH 5.4 (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is an inference to explain the crystallization behavior.

claim: The 2D crystals contained both full-length ExbB and ExbD.
source: The 2D crystals contained both full-length ExbB and ExbD (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is based on SDS-PAGE analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Loss of ExbD occurred in 3D crystals.
source: In contrast, loss of ExbD occurred in 3D crystals (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is based on SDS-PAGE analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C.

claim: The 3D crystals appeared to be built by stacking of 2D crystal layers.
source: The 3D crystals appeared to be built by stacking of 2D crystal layers (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is an observation from the crystal structures shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The periplasmic part of ExbD, which includes a long loop and a compact peptidoglycan-binding motif, would be difficult to fit between the 2D crystal layers in both P21 and P1 3D crystal lattices without deforming these domains.
source: The periplasmic part of ExbD, which includes a long loop and a compact peptidoglycan-binding motif, would be difficult to fit between the 2D crystal layers in both P21 and P1 3D crystal lattices without deforming these domains (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural analysis.

claim: Stacking of 2D crystal layers might exclude ExbD because of steric effects.
source: Thus, stacking of 2D crystal layers might exclude ExbD because of these steric effects.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the loss of ExbD in 3D crystals.

claim: The measurement of the single channel conductance showed that there are two major conductance states at both pH 7.5 and at pH 4.5, exhibiting conductances of 140–150 pS and ~60 pS.
source: The measurement of the single channel conductance showed that there are two major conductance states at both pH 7.5 and at pH 4.5, exhibiting conductances of 140–150 pS and ~60 pS (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from electrophysiology measurements shown in Figure 3.

claim: The frequency of the high conductance state was about 2.6 times that of the low at pH 7.5 (47 events versus 18).
source: The frequency of the high conductance state was about 2.6 times that of the low at pH 7.5 (47 events versus 18)
evidence: This is a quantitative result from electrophysiology measurements.

claim: The frequency of the high conductance state was about half that of the low at pH 4.5 (19 events versus 37).
source: was about half that of the low at pH 4.5 (19 events versus 37).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from electrophysiology measurements.

claim: Two distinct states co-exist and frequency distributions depend on pH, tying in with the EM data if the hexamer and pentamer represent channels with high and low conductance, respectively.
source: Thus two distinct states co-exist and frequency distributions depend on pH, tying in with the EM data if the hexamer and pentamer represent channels with high and low conductance, respectively.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the electrophysiology and EM data.

claim: The two states/channels appear interchangeable in the lipid bilayer as macroscopic currents are reversible on adjusting pH.
source: The two states/channels appear interchangeable in the lipid bilayer as macroscopic currents are reversible on adjusting pH (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is based on electrophysiology data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: A 3D structure of the hexameric complex was determined at 6.7 Å resolution.
source: Starting from a reference map filtered to 30 Å resolution from the atomic model of the ExbB hexamer, a 3D structure was determined at 6.7 Å resolution (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C) with Bayesian-based algorisms implemented in RELION (Scheres, 2012).
evidence: This is a primary result of the cryo-EM analysis.

claim: The cryo-EM map clearly resolves all α-helices and loops in the ExbB hexamer except for small parts of the loops at the periplasmic and at the cytoplasmic ends.
source: Nonetheless, the map clearly resolves all α-helices and loops in the ExbB hexamer except for small parts of the loops at the periplasmic and at the cytoplasmic ends (Figures 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This describes the quality of the cryo-EM map shown in the figures.

claim: Densities corresponding to bound detergent around the TM region are visible at a lower contour level.
source: Densities corresponding to bound detergent around the TM region are visible at a lower contour level (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM map shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The cryo-EM map reveals three rod-like densities inside the channel, which likely correspond to the TM helices of three ExbD molecules.
source: The map also reveals three rod-like densities inside the channel, which likely correspond to the TM helices of three ExbD molecules (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 6.

claim: The helices fit snugly into the hexamer channel, with the arrangement off-centre and asymmetrical.
source: The helices fit snugly into the hexamer channel, with the arrangement off-centre and asymmetrical.
evidence: This describes the arrangement of ExbD helices in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The rod-like densities disappear if 3-fold symmetry is enforced.
source: Indeed, the rod-like densities disappear if 3-fold symmetry is enforced.
evidence: This is an observation from symmetry analysis during cryo-EM reconstruction.
